hints: Differentiate $\ln(x + y) = 3x^2y$ implicitly with respect to $x$.
Substitute $x = 1, y = 0$ into the differentiated equation and solve for $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate both sides of $\ln(x + y) = 3x^2y$ implicitly with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[\ln(x + y)] = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[3x^2y]$$

Apply the chain rule to the left-hand side:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[\ln(x + y)] = \dfrac{1}{x + y}\left(1 + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)$$

Apply the product rule to the right-hand side:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[3x^2y] = 6xy + 3x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$

Substitute the coordinates of the point $(x, y) = (1, 0)$:
$$x + y = 1 + 0 = 1$$
$$\dfrac{1}{1}\left(1 + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) = 6(1)(0) + 3(1)^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$1 + \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0 + 3\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
